title: Provenance manifest
description: The shape of data/curated/manifest.json, the build's account of the cached bytes it read and the entity files it emitted (spec D2, D7, R8, R9). This file is the contract: `readManifest` validates a committed manifest against it before comparing anything, and the build validates the manifest it is about to write. `entities` must name every emitted file once, in the build's OUTPUTS order; `payloads` must name every cached payload the build read once, sorted by cache-relative path. `entityDigest` is recomputed from `entities` rather than trusted. `fetchedAt` is the only timestamp in the dataset, and is absent for a body-only payload with no sidecar.

format.description: The manifest's own format marker, so a reader can refuse a version it does not know.

entityDigest.description: sha256 over `entities` in the build's OUTPUTS order: for each file, `${file}\t${sha256}\t${records}\n`. Recomputed by the reader, never trusted as an opaque string.

entities.description: One entry per emitted entity file, in the build's OUTPUTS order (the order the writer writes and the digest is defined on).

records.description: Non-empty JSONL lines: the record count, so a reader can sanity-check a file.

sha256.description: sha256 of the emitted file's bytes.

payloads.description: One entry per cached payload the build read, sorted by cache-relative path so a diff shows an added or removed payload in one line.

file.description: Path relative to the cache root, e.g. `lol-fandom/cargoexport/Tournaments/<key>.json.gz`. Bodies are gzip-compressed; `bodySha256` is the hash of the uncompressed body (the source's bytes), so the pin describes the response rather than this repository's storage choice.

table.description: The Cargo table whose directory the payload sits in; this is how the build routed it.

endpoint.description: The Cargo endpoint the payload came from.

bodySha256.description: sha256 of the body bytes on disk, verified against the sidecar when there is one.

fetchedAt.description: The sidecar's recorded fetch time, as an ISO-8601 instant. Absent for a body-only payload; the only timestamp in the dataset (spec D8).

status.description: The sidecar's recorded HTTP status. Absent for a body-only payload.

query.description: The query the sidecar records: what produced these bytes. Absent for a body-only payload.
